subject: SLA credit & latency SLO mitigation — Celeron AI
messages:
From: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@celeron.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.example>
Cc: support@celeron.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service incident impacting latency / request for credit

Hi Aditya —

Following todays' incident I wanted to capture what we saw on our side and start the conversation about credits and a short-term SLO tolerance. Between 09:45–12:10 PDT our production traffic experienced elevated latencies and several 500s. Our monitoring shows endpoint p95 latency jumped to ~820ms (normal ~200–250ms) and overall uptime for the rolling 30d window dropped to ~99.20% (our contract baseline is 99.95%).

This was user-visible — we saw a 7% reduction in successful completions and several high-priority support tickets. Given the impact, we're asking Redwood for: 
- a service credit applied to July's invoice (we're proposing 25% but open to discussion), and
- a temporary adjustment to the latency SLO for tail percentiles (p95) for the affected window while you roll fixes.

Can you confirm receipt and let me know the internal next steps / timeline for decision? We need something documented for our finance and SRE teams. Attaching a short incident summary from our end (see support@celeron.ai attachment).

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Hayes
Head of Platform — Celeron AI
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.example>
To: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@celeron.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>, support@celeron.ai
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service incident impacting latency / request for credit

Hi Tom —

Thanks for the summary and the attachment — I pulled this into our incident channel. Really sorry for the disruption. We're treating this as P1 on our end. Initial findings from the runtime team point to an autoscaling oversight that caused elevated queueing during the 09:30–11:50 window; a kernel patch and config change were applied at 11:05 and we saw tail latencies return to baseline by ~12:15.

Short term proposal (pending Deal Desk approval):
- One-off invoice credit of 15% for July (applies to hosted usage charges).
- Temporary p95 latency tolerance: allow p95 up to 500ms for the affected 24h window (July 15) with no SLA penalty for that window.
- A technical postmortem and permanent mitigations (autoscale fixes and a safe-mode routing policy) to be delivered by July 24.

I'm looping Marissa (sales ops / deal desk) to start the formal approval. Can you confirm if Celeron will accept a 15% credit if we commit to the technical remediation timeline? Also attaching the draft SLA amendment we'll use if approved.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Draft-SLA-amendment-Celeron-v2.docx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.example>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.example>
Date: Fri, 17 Jul 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Service incident impacting latency / request for credit

Evelyn —

Forwarding for deal desk sign-off. Summary: Celeron (large strategic account, mid-six-figure ARR) reported a production SLO impact on 2026-07-15; uptime fell to ~99.20% on the rolling window and p95 latency peaked ~820ms. Aditya proposes a conservative commercial remedy: 15% one-off credit + temporary p95 tolerance to 500ms for the affected day. They also want documentation for their billing teams.

Why this needs exec: 
- The requested credit territory (they asked 25%) and the non-standard SLO tolerance need an approval above threshold. 
- The account is strategic and we want to maintain momentum on expansion; concessions must be calibrated.

Proposed deal desk recommendation: 
- Approve a 20% invoice credit (split payment: 10% immediate, 10% conditional on the July 24 postmortem and remediation completion).
- Approve a one-time, time-boxed p95 latency tolerance to 500ms for July 15 only. Add a clause: any similar recurrence within 90 days escalates to remediation plan + intensified credits.

Attachments: Celeron-SLO-incident-report-July2026.pdf, Draft-SLA-amendment-Celeron-v2.docx

Can I get your sign-off to present this to Tom and finalize the amendment?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sales Operations / Deal Desk, Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.example>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.example>
Date: Fri, 17 Jul 2026 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Service incident impacting latency / request for credit

Marissa / Aditya —

Thanks for the clear recommendation. I approve the proposed concession with one change: increase the immediate credit to 15% and leave the conditional 5% (total 20%), with the condition tied to delivery of the postmortem and verification of the autoscale fix by July 24 (SRE lead to confirm). The one-time p95 tolerance to 500ms for July 15 is acceptable; include the 90-day recurrence escalation clause as drafted.

Please: 
1) Finalize the SLA amendment (use the attached draft), mark the conditional credit terms, and route to Tom for signature.
2) Copy Legal on the amendment when you send.
3) Have SRE provide a short verification note when they validate remediation (cc: me).

I'll be available if the customer pushes for a larger credit, but prefer to keep concessions tied to demonstrable remediation.

Evelyn Hart
VP, Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference
